text:
sahil: seeing a spike of preemptible evictions in eu-central today, ~22% pool loss in last 4m. Can we run the fast-path runbook? :warning:
elyse: putting checklist here. keep it minimal — goal: restore serving for high-priority routes in <10m.
elyse: FAST-PATH: 1) Protect critical traffic 2) Pause nonessential batch 3) Drain & mark nodes 4) Kick cache warmers 5) Notify oncall/infra team
tom: protecting traffic: toggle routing weight for critical models to dedicated pool (50-100% depending on SLA) via infra API. example: 
```
PUT /v1/route-weight
{ "model":"text-embed-512", "from":"preemptible-eu", "to":"dedicated-eu", "weight": 100, "reason": "preemptible-eviction-spike" }
```
elyse: If we need partial fallback, use 75% -> 25% split to avoid cold start storm.
opscheck-bot: Alert rule: page if region preemptible capacity drop >20% sustained for 3m. Refer to docs/alerts/preemptible-loss
infra-oncall-bot: oncall notified: @oncall-eng-sre
sahil: pause noncritical batch jobs: set spot autoscaler to suspend scale-ups and decrease desired by 30%
tom: command to scale deployment down for batch namespace:
```
kubectl -n batch set resources deployment/batch-worker --limits=cpu=0 --replicas=2
```
elyse: node handling: cordon nodes then drain with short grace period (2m) to speed eviction handling but try to checkpoint before restart.
elyse: node commands:
```
kubectl get nodes -l pool=preemptible-eu -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon
kubectl drain NODE-NAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120
```
tom: if pods hold onto GPU contexts and won't exit, use our checkpoint API to snapshot kv state before forced restart:
```
curl -X POST "$CHECKPOINT_API/snapshot?pod=<pod>" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
sahil: networking note: last time evictions correlated with transient network errors in the eu-central AZ B. Check subnet-route metrics and VPC flow logs if we see node Liveness flaps.
elyse: quick checks (run in parallel):
- provider meta: gcloud compute instance-operations list --filter="status=TERMINATED AND labels:preemptible"
- k8s: kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep Evicted
- autoscaler: kubectl describe hpa -n infra | grep -A3 preemptible
- metrics: grafana link: https://grafana.internal/r/d/Preemptible/region-eu

opscheck-bot: suggestion: run warmup job to rehydrate model KV cache after routing change. Use warmup image with 25% concurrency for 2 minutes.
tom: warmup k8s job example: 
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: kv-warmup-eu
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: warmer
        image: infra/kv-warmer:stable
        args: ["--targets=critical-models","--rate=50"]
      restartPolicy: Never
```
elyse: cost considerations: fallback to dedicated increases cost by ~3.5x token price for our current fleet. Prefer using warm dedicated capacity (pre-warmed, lower multiplier) over cold on-demand. log cost delta in incident ticket.
sahil: escalation thresholds: open SEV if >30% region capacity lost for >5m OR SLA error rate >8% for 10m. Otherwise handle as infra incident.
elyse: post-incident actions to add to playbook:
- add automated routing rule when drop >=12% in 2m
- quarterly chaos test: simulate 25% AZ preemptible loss in eu-central
- add a provider-metadata collector to incident dashboards
- run cost impact report (tokens/sec * fallback_multiplier) for incident window

deploy-bot: non-critical pipelines paused: batch-ci, perf-tests :white_check_mark:
opscheck-bot: leaving a checklist item: ensure 95th percentile latency < SLA within 10m of routing change
tom: status update: switched critical routes to dedicated at 60%. Starting KV warmup. Monitoring error rate.
sahil: thanks — once stable we'll escalate to postmortem and capture exact preemption metadata. moving this thread to incidents for DEBRIEF.
elyse: will add timelines and metrics to the incident doc (error rate, preemptible nodes lost, cost multiplier).
infra-oncall-bot: incident channel created: #incidents/preemptible-eu-1842504321
sahil: tagging ops: @platform-ops please review routing automation proposal in follow-up.
